verses.note: The first fear in Scripture is the terror of a guilty conscience, which drives the sinner away from God. The Bible later speaks of a different fear of the LORD, reverent trust that draws near, and the New Testament speaks of love that casts out fear (1 John 4:18).
Pagan courtiers respond to God's warning with the fear Abraham denied them. Scripture often shows outsiders fearing God more readily than his own people, as with the sailors in Jonah 1:16.

The verse assumes that a people without the fear of God is capable of anything, and in that Abraham is right. His mistake is to assume he can tell who fears God by their nationality. Fear of man drove him to lie, the snare Proverbs 29:25 warns of.
The fear of God is defined here by what a person will not withhold from him. It is reverence shown in action, the same quality for which Job is described as one who feared God (Job 1:1).

The encounter produces fear before it produces worship. Jacob's fear is not terror of punishment but the awe of a man who suddenly knows himself in God's presence, the beginning of wisdom in Proverbs 9:10.
